# Final editorial sweep — 2 October 2026

Baseline: production tree deployed from merge commit 4742a4ce073302a281c1afe7aac48ce3211fd8da.

## Scope

- Reviewed all 102 HTML pages for duplicated long-form passages, missing titles, descriptions and H1s, invalid JSON-LD, promotional phrasing and language left over from earlier article versions.
- Compared every blog-index card with the destination article's current H1 and meta description.
- Reviewed the eight pace-band preset pages for duplication and usefulness. They retain repeated operating instructions because each is a working preset, while each page also contains a target-specific calculation or decision.
- Preserved routes, canonicals, calculator behaviour and the original race-data article.

## Changes

- Synchronised blog cards with the edited articles so summaries no longer repeat superseded claims.
- Rewrote promotional or overconfident titles and descriptions around GPS pacing, hills, marathon-pace workouts, cardiac drift, wind, heat, adrenaline and late-race slowing.
- Replaced claims such as “proven”, “real causes”, “prevent”, “actually works” and “blow-up” where the page could not establish them.
- Corrected the repeated article error “a illustrative” to “an illustrative”.
- Corrected an unclear tangent-running sentence and made its safety and crowd context explicit.
- Aligned Open Graph and Twitter titles and descriptions with the visible article title and current meta description.
- Updated modified dates only on articles substantively edited in this pass.

## Deliberate limits

- No new article was added. The stronger improvement was consistency between existing articles, their index cards and their social and structured summaries.
- Repeated calculator instructions and legal or medical limits remain where they are necessary for safe, correct use.
- The review improves originality, clarity and transparency; it cannot guarantee an advertising-platform decision.
